question: Which among the following is a book authored by Jeet Thayil?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Low**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The book titled **Low** is a novel authored by the acclaimed Indian writer **Jeet Thayil**, published in **2020**.
 
• The story follows the protagonist, **Dominic Ullis**, a poet who travels from **New York** to **Mumbai** following the death of his wife to scatter her ashes.
 
• The novel is noted for its deep dive into the **urban underbelly** of **Mumbai**, exploring themes of **grief**, **drug addiction**, and **nihilism** over the course of a single weekend.
 
• **Jeet Thayil** utilizes a hallucinatory prose style in **Low**, which serves as a spiritual successor to his debut novel, **Narcopolis**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Low.***
 
• **Jeet Thayil** is a multidisciplinary artist born in **1959** in **Kerala**, known for his work as a **poet**, **novelist**, and **musician**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fury**:

 
 
• This novel was authored by **Salman Rushdie** and published in the year **2001**.
 
• It is set in **New York City** and centers around **Malik Solanka**, a historian of ideas and a world-famous doll maker who is struggling with uncontrollable **rage**.
 
• The book examines the consumerist culture of **America** at the turn of the millennium.
 
 
 
• **Shame**:
 
 
• Published in **1983**, **Shame** is another significant work by **Salman Rushdie**.
 
• It is a **political satire** that serves as an allegory for the political turmoil in **Pakistan**, focusing on the lives of characters representing **Zulfikar Ali Bhutto** and **General Zia-ul-Haq**.
 
• The novel won the **French Prix du Meilleur Livre Étranger** and was shortlisted for the **Booker Prize**.
 
 
 
• **Countdown**:
 
 
• **Countdown** is a non-fiction book written by the renowned author **Amitav Ghosh**, published in **1999**.
 
• The book provides a critical analysis of the **nuclear tests** conducted by **India** at **Pokhran** in **May 1998**.
 
• It features interviews with various people in **India**, **Pakistan**, and **Nepal**, discussing the implications of **nuclearization** in **South Asia**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Jeet Thayil's Literary Achievements**:

 
 
• His first novel, **Narcopolis** (**2012**), was shortlisted for the prestigious **Man Booker Prize** and won the **DSC Prize for South Asian Literature**.
 
• He was awarded the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **2012** for his poetry collection titled **These Errors Are Correct**.
 
• He is also the editor of **The Bloodaxe Book of Contemporary Indian Poets** (**2008**), a significant anthology of Indian English poetry.
 
 
 
• **Themes in Thayil's Work**:
 
 
• His writing often reflects his personal history and experiences in **Mumbai** and **New York**, frequently touching upon **modernity**, **loss**, and **human vulnerability**.
 
• His background as a **songwriter** and **guitarist** often influences the **rhythmic quality** of his prose and verse.
